$comment: Project config for Telcoin (TEL). Every address here is copied from config/chains.json / src/lib/telContracts.ts / scripts/lib/staking.js (verified in docs/TEL-CONTRACTS.md). Long wallet lists stay in their existing config files (classification.*). Pipelines still read config/chains.json directly; this file is the multi-token view of the same facts.
name: Telcoin
description: Telcoin: legacy TEL (2 decimals) and TEL v3 (18 decimals) on Ethereum, Polygon and Base, counted together against a fixed 100B supply.

data.$comment: legacyRoot: this project's pipelines still write to public/data/ (pre-multi-token layout). The site serves it at /data/tel/* and /live-data/tel/* regardless. Flip to false once the scripts write public/data/tel/ directly.

treasury.$comment: labelEras: treasury-history rows dated before `before` were written when these TELx reward contracts were category council (relabelled to staking in #78). The backfill replays such rows with the old label so anchor, target and validation rows agree.

anchorAdjustments.note: The 2026-09-29 holders snapshot omitted TELx Council, which held 56,689,486 TEL v3 on Polygon (40,710,105 at 2026-10-23 plus 1,546,392 and 14,432,990 sent to 0x7e1c409d... at blocks 94723978 and 95121949). Backfill adds this to that row in memory only.

pipeline.$comment: Ported pipeline scripts read chain/token/contract addresses from chainsConfig (TEL keeps config/chains.json, which also carries explorerApi settings). A project without chainsConfig gets its chain map derived from chains[] below (scripts/lib/projects.js deriveChainsFromProject).

supply.note: legacy + v3 = 100B; legacy retired into v3 via TokenMigration/MigrationVault is netted out, Polygon/Base legacy mirrors are backed by Ethereum bridge locks (docs/TEL-CONTRACTS.md, Supply accounting).

holders.$comment: Holder-tier settings (scripts/lib/holderTiers.js, src/lib/holderTiers.ts). TEL's values are the historical pipeline constants (RETAIL_THRESHOLD, MEGA_HOLDER_THRESHOLD, BALANCE_RANGES, DISTRIBUTION_RANGES, CONCENTRATION_BUCKETS) and equal config/holder-tiers.default.json. Distribution tier labels are join keys into holder-transitions/tier-outflows/holders-history — do not rename.

gated.$comment: Wallet-level forensics stay behind the forensics gate (netlify/functions/forensics-gate.cjs; password today, paywall later). walletFlows feeds scripts/generate-wallet-flows.js: data/forensics/ for TEL (legacyRoot), data/<slug>/forensics/ for other projects. See docs/MULTI-TOKEN.md "Gated forensics".

copy.$comment: TEL-only facts for UI copy. Overrides the generic glossary template for a term id (src/lib/glossary.ts). `methodology` overrides a methodology hover-card section (src/lib/methodology.ts); its link hrefs use {token:<chain>:<generation>} / {explorer:<chain>}. Placeholders {ticker} {name} {chains} {supply} are filled from this file.

legacy-v3.definition: {name} upgraded {ticker} to a new contract (v3, 18 decimals, same address on {chains}). Holders swap 1:1. Balances here add legacy + v3 so an upgrade never looks like a sale, and total supply stays at {supply}.

supply.definition: The fixed {ticker} supply. Bridged copies on Polygon and Base are backed by tokens locked on Ethereum, and swapped legacy {ticker} is retired, so each token is counted once.

cex.definition: Centralised exchange (e.g. KuCoin, MEXC). CEX balance is {ticker} sitting in exchange-controlled wallets. Moving {ticker} to an exchange is often, but not always, a step before selling.

dex.definition: Decentralised exchange (e.g. Uniswap, Balancer, ParaSwap). {ticker} in DEX pools is liquidity that traders buy from and sell into.

escrow.definition: {ticker} held by custodians (BitGo, Anchorage) or migration contracts. It is not circulating and is excluded from retail figures.

staked.definition: {ticker} locked in the {name} staking contract. Stakers must unstake before upgrading to v3, so staking can fall during the migration.

text.cex.balance.info: {ticker} held in known exchange wallets. Additional balances may exist in untagged wallets, so treat this as a floor, not a total. A one-time ~8.7B step-up is a re-labelling of previously vault-held KuCoin wallets, not an inflow.
text.holders.cex.info:
{ticker} sitting in known exchange wallets. An exchange hot wallet is one commingled pool that backs all of that exchange's customers' {ticker} balances — it's mostly customer funds held in custody, not the exchange's own.

Trading on an exchange happens in its private off-chain ledger, so on-chain we can't see whether any of this has been sold, nor how many people hold it. A rising balance means more {ticker} positioned near the market; a falling balance means {ticker} leaving exchanges (often to self-custody or staking).

Note: a one-time ~8.7B step-up reflects re-labelling seven previously vault-held KuCoin wallets into CEX Custody — not an inflow.
text.holders.retailHeld.info:
{ticker} held in ordinary wallets — everything except exchange custody, Association treasury, Telcoin Holdings, escrow, bridges and DEX liquidity.

Shown separately from CEX Balance rather than blended into one total, because the two moving in opposite directions is the signal: {ticker} leaving exchanges for self-custody is accumulation, the reverse is supply moving toward the market. A combined figure stays flat through both.

Staked {ticker}, including the Staked (v3) StakingModule portion, is already inside this figure (credited to each staker's wallet), not added on top.
text.holders.held.info: {ticker} in retail wallets compared with {ticker} in custody at known exchange wallets. All chains combined. Retail includes {stakedTotal} staked {ticker}, of which {stakedV3} is in the v3 StakingModule (credited to each staker's wallet, so it isn't counted twice).
text.holders.staked.info: {ticker} staked on Polygon: the legacy staking contract plus the v3 StakingModule (live since 1 Sep 2026), counted once per staker. It's a subset of Retail Held (already counted there, including the v3 portion), shown separately as a measure of long-term conviction. Staked {ticker} can't be sold until unstaked.
text.staking.intro: {ticker} staked by retail in the legacy staking contract and the v3 StakingModule, mapped back to holder wallets and counted once per staker (excludes exchange & hot wallets).
text.supply.association.description: Treasury and council / ops Safes — Association-controlled custody, listed together in the hero bucket. Balances checked on-chain.
text.supply.holdings.description: Confirmed Holdings wallets ({amount} {ticker}): reserves, shared Safes, bridge-hub, and Base ops/cold custody.
text.supply.escrow.description: {ticker} held by third-party custodians under a SAFE
text.supply.coingecko.note: CoinGecko's figure isn't a different methodology — it's the main treasury wallet's exact on-chain balance right after its 2025-10-01 transfer to Anchorage, never refreshed since. Every treasury move after that date{treasuryNow} is invisible to their number.
text.treasury.history.info:
Daily balances reconstructed from on-chain Transfer logs, one line per group.

The two "Association —" lines are subsets of ONE entity, the Telcoin Association: its Treasury address, and its TAO / council / ops Safes. The pie above combines them into a single Association bucket, so it shows one figure where this chart shows two.

Telcoin Holdings is a SEPARATE entity, not part of the Association, and the two are never combined into a single figure.

Escrow is third-party custody (BitGo, Anchorage) plus five assumed Holdings-funded vaults — not discretionary supply, and hidden by default because it dwarfs the rest.
text.walletFlows.locked.supply: Supply split by entity: Telcoin treasury, Holdings and Association, escrow, exchanges, DEX pools and retail

circulatingSupply.how: This box shows CoinGecko's reported circulating supply (~95.08B), not a figure we compute. It is not a different accounting method — it's a frozen snapshot. The main treasury wallet held exactly 4,922,764,633 TEL immediately after sending 2.5B to Anchorage Digital Vault on 2025-10-01; CoinGecko's implied non-circulating amount (100B minus their reported figure) is 4,922,763,633 — within 1,000 TEL, the size of a routine test transfer that precedes it. CoinGecko read that balance once around that date and has not updated it since. Every treasury transaction after 2025-10-01 — including the escrow funding into BitGo a month later, and payouts down to treasury's actual balance today — is invisible to their number. The Tokenomics page's Supply Breakdown reconstructs circulating supply directly from on-chain balances instead.
circulatingSupply.verify: Open the treasury wallet on Etherscan and read its Transfer history: the balance right after its 2025-10-01 transfer to Anchorage Digital Vault matches CoinGecko's implied carve-out to within 1,000 TEL.

holderSnapshot.how: Every wallet's TEL balance is reconstructed from the token's on-chain Transfer event logs on Ethereum, Polygon and Base — read directly from full nodes, the same ledger the block explorers use — then staking is added from the Polygon staking contracts (legacy and v3 StakingModule). A holder is any wallet with a non-zero balance, with no minimum applied: that includes roughly 9,500 wallets holding less than 1 TEL each (a few thousand TEL between all of them). They are counted in the headline and in the smallest distribution tier alike, so every holder count on this page reconciles to the same total. A wallet's balance is its legacy TEL (2 decimals) plus its upgraded TEL v3 (18 decimals, 0x7E13…0731 on every chain), each read with its own decimals. Telcoin's official upgrade swaps legacy for v3 1:1: the upgrade contract locks the legacy TEL and mints the same amount of v3 to the holder, so the locked legacy TEL is left out and the v3 is counted instead — nothing is counted twice, and the total stays 100B.
holderSnapshot.verify: Open the TEL token contract on any explorer and check the Holders tab, or look up any single wallet's TEL balance directly.

balanceInsights.how: Average, median, percentiles and the Gini coefficient are computed over the reconstructed on-chain balances of retail wallets (exchange & hot wallets excluded).
balanceInsights.verify: Balances come straight from the TEL token contract — spot-check any wallet's holdings on the explorer.

concentration.how: Retail wallets are ranked by balance and the top-N cohorts' combined holdings summed. Exchange & hot wallets are excluded so a custody pool is never counted as a whale.
concentration.verify: The token's Holders tab on the explorer lists every wallet by balance, largest first.

holderMomentum.how: Holder counts and first-time wallets are derived from weekly on-chain snapshots of every wallet holding >0 TEL.
holderMomentum.verify: The Holders count on the token contract page reflects the same on-chain set.

staking.how: Staked TEL combines two contracts on Polygon: the legacy Telcoin staking contract and the TEL v3 StakingModule (live since 1 Sep 2026, block 93,048,895). Both are read on-chain and mapped back to each staker's wallet; a wallet staked in both is counted once as a staker, with its two amounts added. Staked TEL is already part of each staker's retail balance, so it is never added on top of Retail Held. The module's positions aren't in the archived daily snapshots, so its history can't be rebuilt: before 1 Sep 2026 it held nothing (the legacy figure is the whole total), and between then and the first measured date its balance is unknown and left blank rather than guessed. Changes that start in that window show a dagger (†) instead of a number.
staking.verify: Open either contract on Polygonscan to inspect staked positions and transactions.

overlap.how: Wallets that hold TEL on more than one chain are matched by address across the per-chain snapshots.
overlap.verify: Look up the same wallet address on each chain's explorer to see its balance on each.

cexFlows.how: Deposits to and withdrawals from known exchange hot wallets are counted directly from TEL Transfer logs. Trading happens off-chain in the exchange's private ledger, so this shows supply moving toward/away from the market — not realized sales. CEX Balance history is also aligned when wallets are re-labelled (e.g. KuCoin vaults moved into the exchange set): that step is a classification change, not an inflow, and prior days are backfilled so YTD deltas do not treat the re-label as new deposits.
cexFlows.verify: Every exchange wallet is a real on-chain address (expand a row to see them); all transfers to and from it are public on the explorer. Measured netflow below is the on-chain deposit/withdrawal truth when a balance chart step looks like a labelling cliff.

distribution.how: Retail wallets are bucketed by balance range (exchange & hot wallets excluded). Tier movement tracks the SAME wallet across weekly snapshots, and each outgoing transfer is classified from the Transfer logs: into a DEX pool as a swap = sold, into a pool as liquidity provision = added to LP (not a sale), to an exchange wallet = deposit, to another wallet = moved/split. Incoming transfers reverse those labels (bought / unstaked from LP / from exchange / from wallet).
distribution.verify: Balances and every transfer are public on the TEL token contract; the DEX pool and exchange addresses used are themselves on-chain and linkable.

dexSwaps.how: Swaps are counted from TEL Transfer logs into and out of on-chain DEX liquidity pools (QuickSwap, Uniswap). TEL sent into a pool is swapped for another coin (a sale); TEL sent out is a buy. Liquidity provision (adding/removing LP) is tracked separately from swaps — depositing TEL into a pool is not a sale, and withdrawing LP is not a buy.
dexSwaps.verify: Open a pool contract on the explorer to see its TEL transfers in and out — each swap is a public transaction.

supplyBreakdown.how: Total supply is always 100B (the legacy TEL contract on Ethereum, where all of it was minted). Since the TEL v3 upgrade every balance is legacy TEL plus v3 TEL, and the legacy TEL locked in Telcoin's upgrade contract in exchange for minted v3 is left out so it is never counted twice (legacy supply − locked-for-v3 + v3 supply − bridge-locked mirrors = 100B; scripts/verify-tel-supply.js re-derives this from the chains). We split it into simple base-layer buckets anyone can read — retail wallets, DEX liquidity, exchange custody, escrow, Telcoin Association-Controlled Safes (treasury + council/ops), Telcoin Holdings (confirmed Holdings wallets), Other, and In transit (bridges) — so the pieces add to 100B. In transit is mostly TEL locked on Ethereum while it shows up on Polygon or Base — not missing wallets. Circulating excludes treasury + council, plus the escrow that's contractually committed back to treasury under a SAFE (traced on-chain to Telcoin Association funding — see data/escrow-safe-provenance.md; the Escrow detail shows the current split); the rest of escrow stays circulating. CoinGecko’s ~95B is the main treasury wallet's on-chain balance right after its 2025-10-01 transfer to Anchorage, never refreshed since — not a different methodology, just a frozen snapshot (see the Circulating Supply info icon on the home page for the full trace). Click Association, Holdings, Other, or In transit for address-level drill-down. Wallets with an Analysis badge expose a gated deep dive (funding chain, counterparties, controllers) unlocked for admin accounts. After wallet labels change (especially retail vs excluded), run a full holders scrape so Retail, history, transitions, and supply reconciliation stay consistent — incremental scans alone are not enough. Temporary Other detail tags like “large personal wallet” are not the permanent Retail home until that full scrape.
supplyBreakdown.verify: Base layer: the chart and bucket list. Power users can click Association, Holdings, Other, or In transit for address lists, bridge math, and explorer links. Identity notes: data/other-address-identity.md and data/holdings-wallet-analysis.md.
